claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with a homogeneous microstructure and standard surface finish.
The proposed treatment uses boron ion implantation at 20–50 keV and a dose of 1×10^17 ions/cm² at room temperature.
The implantation is followed by annealing at approximately 500°C in an inert atmosphere.
Boron implantation followed by annealing creates a sub-micron modified surface layer.
The modified surface layer contains boride precipitates and an altered near-surface composition.
Annealing promotes controlled boron diffusion and in situ boride formation.
The resulting boride phases are hard and thermally stable.
Boride phases provide a low-shear interface during sliding and thereby reduce friction.
The increased hardness and thermal stability of the boride phases improve wear resistance.
The boride-enriched surface layer acts as a self-lubricating tribolayer.
The treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 20% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The treatment will significantly reduce wear rate relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The friction and wear improvements will persist from room temperature to approximately 600°C.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi has higher friction and accelerated wear because of conventional oxidation and the absence of an engineered lubricious layer.
The treatment may lose effectiveness above approximately 600°C if the boride phases thermally degrade.
Departures from the proposed implantation energy, dose, or annealing conditions may cause inconsistent tribolayer formation.
